items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And if you said an artist is Sammy Davis Jr. Check to see his demeanor and manner. You don’t hear him cursing in front of people.

ctx.x: That’s another thing I wanted to ask you about. The concept, the difference between, as we know it today with pop culture, the difference between an artist and an entertainer. Because when I look at some of the earlier great jazz musicians, to me they were both. What they did it was art, it was beautiful, it was so beautifully constructed, and yet it was entertaining. And now it seems like we have entertainers that get paid exorbitant amounts of money to sing or play about things that don’t have much merit. There…

Well it’s a little more sophisticated. And I think lazy people don’t like jazz because they don’t want to take the time to really find out anything about it. How can I address that? Well it made me think of one thing, and I’ll come back to your question. But one time I had to deal with sidemen versus artists. Or getting sidemen to look at themselves like artists. Sidemen might be just a person like myself. I was in a big band and I got a chance to play solos here and there. I became aware of the difference…

You know Madonna was signed to a contract for 60 million dollars here about a year ago. And I don’t begrudge people their success, but I, when, you know I’ve won some cultural grants. And whenever I won a grant, at the end of the grant period I have to fill out all these things about how I spent the money and what I did and how it helped the community and what kind of people it reached and who I hired. I have to account for every dollar. You know what I mean? And I would just like to see there be some sense of ©…

items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 16, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I think I’ve done some things with Sammy Davis Jr. and so forth.

ctx.x: You don’t get that many. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

I was assured of playing the bridge of “April in Paris” with Basie’s band, because sometimes there was a lot of things we had with Judy Garland. It was so funny, I was watching a show the other night, well I was watching this film clip that somebody sent to me, Judy Garland, Mel Torme, and I think it might have been The Sammy Davis Jr. Show, that was done in Brooklyn like 1964 or something. But anyway, they played “April in Paris,” and I was getting all set to see myself play my little bridge, Mel Torme sang it.…
You’re making up for — I guess everything comes around. I wanted to fill in a couple of holes in your history here. I know that you have worked with a familiar name, King Kolax?
